text.p: Harvesting of Oklahoma's wheat crop was complete as of Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
The service said on its weekly crop progress report that wheat harvesting was 100 percent complete, on par with 1996 and slightly ahead of the five-year average of 99 percent.
Corn tasseling advanced to 55 percent compared to 97 percent last year and 82 percent on average.
The report said corn producers in the Panhandle district were concerned that the extreme hot conditions could interfere with pollination.
Corn was rated 94 percent in good to excellent condition, ahead of 93 percent in that category a week ago.

Beneficial rains fell over sorghum-growing areas, but dryland sorghum in the Panhandle area was in need of more moisture. Sorghum was rated 64 percent in good to excellent condition, against 76 percent at that level last week.

Cotton was rated 76 percent in good to excellent condition, below 77 percent at that level last week. Nine percent of cotton acreage was setting bolls, lagging 31 percent last year and 19 percent on average.
